Title: Use the official GitHub CLI packages and repos as the default install path
Description: The source repeatedly distinguishes recommended (official) installation methods — Debian/apt, RPM repos, Homebrew and precompiled binaries — and states these packages “are supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers” with updates “powered by GitHub CLI deployment workflow.” The central editorial claim: prefer the official packages and repos published on cli.github.com as the primary installation and upgrade method for gh.
Audience: Developers, sysadmins, and Linux distro maintainers who install or manage GitHub CLI (gh) on Linux/BSD systems.
Rationale: This idea focuses on a single, high-value recommendation grounded in the document: the project itself marks specific packaging channels as recommended and maintained. Explaining what the source explicitly endorses (and why that matters for update cadence, maintenance responsibility, and reproducible installs) is directly supported by the text and helpful to readers deciding where to get gh.
Evidence: Explicit statements in the source: “Debian packages are hosted on the GitHub CLI marketing site… These packages are supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers with updates powered by GitHub CLI deployment workflow.” Similarly, RPM and Homebrew sections repeat that packages “are supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers.” The document provides concrete install instructions for apt, dnf/dnf4/dnf5, yum, zypper, brew and links to precompiled binaries at https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/latest.
